teams.heading: Fiji enter talks with Warren Gatland as Shaun Edwards is linked
teams.body: Fiji are reportedly in talks with former Wales boss Warren Gatland over their head coach vacancy, with defensive mastermind Shaun Edwards also linked to the setup. Gatland has entered a two-horse race for the 2027 Rugby World Cup cycle alongside former Springboks coach Jake White, who remains a strong favourite. The Fiji Rugby Union is whittling down a shortlist of 31 applicants to succeed Mick Byrne, aiming to make an appointment before November's Nations Championship matches.

lead.why: Fiji entering talks with Warren Gatland and the link to Shaun Edwards represents a significant new development in the head coaching search.

teams.heading: England midfielders Max Ojomoh, Joe Marchant, and Will Joseph impress Borthwick
teams.body: A trio of English centres have caught the eye during the latest round of club action, sending what analysts describe as 'necessary signals' to Steve Borthwick. Max Ojomoh, Joe Marchant and Will Joseph each produced standout performances across the weekend, with Marchant’s defensive work in particular earning praise for his 20-tackle effort. While these displays offer the England head coach tactical options in the midfield, recent injury concerns across the professional game continue to dent the depth available for the upcoming autumn campaign.

teams.heading: Bordeaux-Begles cement top-tier status as England greats snub Super Rugby
teams.body: Bordeaux-Begles have been identified as a superior 'whole package' outfit compared to their southern hemisphere counterparts in a new ranking compiled by former England internationals Dan Cole and Ben Youngs. The double-winning Investec Champions Cup champions featured prominently in the analysis, which critically evaluated the current standard of Super Rugby Pacific. While the New Zealand-based Hurricanes were debated, the panel ultimately excluded them from the top 10, favouring the consistency and quality of the Top 14 teams.

teams.heading: Owen Doyle condemns Michael Hooper and Sir Steve Hansen regarding Piardi
teams.body: Former IRFU director of referees Owen Doyle has publicly criticised remarks made by Michael Hooper and Sir Steve Hansen concerning Italian official Andrea Piardi. The former Test referee dismissed the duo's recent suggestions that Piardi should no longer officiate matches involving Australia, labelling the commentary as "totally out of order." Doyle defended the official's performance during the recent Wallabies-Springboks fixture, arguing that the officiating controversy stemmed from external communication failures rather than the referee’s decision-making on the pitch.

lead.why: It reports a prominent figure in Irish rugby governance publicly weighing in on a contentious international officiating debate.

teams.heading: Italy men’s side prepare for South Africa in Nations Championship round
teams.body: Italy are set to face South Africa in Round 4 of the Nations Championship. The Azzurri last met the reigning world champions in November 2025, where the match finished in a 32-14 defeat for Italy. Head coach Gonzalo Quesada’s side continues their campaign following a challenging period in the competition, seeking to improve on their current standing after three opening rounds.

teams.heading: Lucia Scott returns as Scotland women finalise WXV tour squad
teams.body: The Scotland women’s squad sees the return of Lucia Scott for the upcoming WXV Global Series tests against Australia. Interim head coach Dave Butcher has also included uncapped players Nicole Flynn and Imogen Spence for the tour, which concludes with matches on 17 and 23 October. While Rachel Phillips is back following concussion protocols, the team will be without the injured duo of Alex Stewart and Emma Wassell as they look to conclude their series fixtures down under.

teams.heading: Josh Adams eyes third World Cup as he nears playing return
teams.body: Wales wing Josh Adams has declared his determination to feature in a third consecutive World Cup, with the tournament in Australia now exactly one year away. Despite missing the summer defeat to South Africa with a calf injury, the 31-year-old is closing in on a return to action for Cardiff. “I am training, but it’s important that you navigate your way through correctly and there’s no rush,” Adams said. He is currently focused on regaining full fitness for international duty.

lead.why: Josh Adams' explicit target of a third World Cup is a major positive narrative for the men's national team.

teams.heading: Argentina spearheads ambitious four-nation proposal to host 2035 World Cup
teams.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has officially submitted a joint bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup alongside Uruguay, Chile, and Brazil. If successful, the tournament would be the first to be staged in South America, with matches proposed for venues including the Monumental and José Amalfitani in Buenos Aires. UAR President Félix Páez Molina stated the candidacy represents a "very important step" for the region, which offers a combined population of 283 million and proven experience hosting major international sporting events.

teams.heading: Fraser McReight reflects on 'tough conversations' with All Blacks boss Rennie
teams.body: Wallabies back-rower Fraser McReight has opened up on the challenging feedback he received from former Australia head coach Dave Rennie during his early Test career. Now a 46-cap regular under Les Kiss, McReight credited those difficult early dialogues with helping him understand the preparation required for international rugby. As he prepares to face Rennie’s New Zealand side this weekend, McReight insisted that while Australia possess the belief to compete, they must remain focused on the tactical threats the hosts will pose.

teams.heading: Ryan Lonergan credits Japanese player Kaito Shigeno for passing consistency
teams.body: Wallabies scrum-half Ryan Lonergan has revealed that his refined passing technique is the result of using specialist grip tape recommended by Kaito Shigeno. The pair connected while playing for the Barbarians in 2023, where Lonergan observed the Japanese half-back applying the tape to improve his grip. Lonergan now utilizes the method exclusively during matches to maintain consistency in wet conditions, noting that he sources the specific tape whenever he visits Japan for fixtures.

teams.heading: Kieran Read urges Dave Rennie to build loose trio around Lakai
teams.body: Former captain Kieran Read has identified Peter Lakai as the player the All Blacks must centre their back-row around for the upcoming Bledisloe Cup Tests. With Ardie Savea and Luke Jacobson sidelined due to injury, Read suggested that the team's loose forward combinations have lacked the time to solidify, noting that the pack is not yet settled on its best starting configuration. Read argued that Lakai offers the potential to provide the necessary stability to the All Blacks' loose forward unit.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield claims Wallabies outplayed Springboks where All Blacks were weak
teams.body: Former Springbok lock Victor Matfield has warned that the Wallabies managed to outplay the Springboks in specific areas where New Zealand struggled during the recent Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series. Matfield noted that while South Africa secured the series victory by winning the big moments, New Zealand’s inability to make the right decisions under pressure was a deciding factor. He suggests the All Blacks may look to rectify these tactical shortcomings in their upcoming Bledisloe Cup fixture against Australia.

lead.why: It provides tactical analysis from a former Springbok great regarding the team's recent form.
